first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, so simplifying onboarding is the most direct intervention with potential to improve sustainable adoption without immediately sacrificing price or margin. Verify memory_86 because it is central to the proposed action but its archived evidence must be checked for durable qualified-revenue impact. Verify memory_73 because aggressive competitor pricing makes promotional pricing consequential, yet discounting may attract lower-value accounts and is an important alternative to rule in or out. Use a guarded test with downstream qualified-revenue and retention measures, not completion alone.

final.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified evidence shows a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, directly addressing both current onboarding and activation declines. Signup simplification and in-product activation messaging provide supporting evidence. Do not use promotional pricing as the primary intervention: although it lifted qualified revenue 18% initially, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Measure qualified revenue, activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, and renewal-intent guardrails alongside completion so short-term adoption gains do not mask downstream value loss.
